title: Transport & Key Handoff Review - Hightide Shipping
summary: High-level review of encryption in transit and at rest, BYOK/HSM handoff options, audit logging requirements, and residency constraints. Decision leaning toward hybrid model with customer-managed keys (BYOK) using an HSM-backed KMS, plus mutual TLS for service-to-service traffic. Redwood to provide SOC2/ISO docs and a proposed runbook for key rotation and emergency key handoff.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 + ISO artifacts and network zoning diagram by 2026-01-21
Redwood to draft BYOK HSM runbook and sample KMS key policy by 2026-01-25
Schedule on-prem connector deep dive w/ Aria and Evan week of 2026-01-26
action_items: Jordan Meyers: Share SOC2 and ISO packages and compliance FAQ :2026-01-21
Aria Singh: Produce BYOK/HSM runbook draft and sample key policy :2026-01-25
Evan Cole: Provide network diagram and list of regions with residency constraints :2026-01-20
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-18 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Aria (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood PM), Carlos (Hightide Head of Security), Priya (Platform Lead), Evan (DevOps)

[00:00:02] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick run of the agenda, uh encryption in transit, at rest, keys, and the handoff path. Aria will cover the HSM/BYOK options and Liam will chime on audit logging.

[00:01:10] Carlos: Great. we, at Hightide, we have two main constraints: 1) data must remain in eu-west-2 for shipment manifests, and 2) keys must be owner-controlled for PII fields - so we are leaning BYOK with HSM.

[00:02:05] Aria: Understood. to confirm, you want an HSM-backed K-M-S where you hold the root/unwrapping key? or were you thinking of a split escrow?

[00:02:22] Priya: Ideally customer-managed root, yes. but we need a safe handoff process for rotation and incident access - we can't be stuck with a single person having to do manual handoffs.

[00:03:10] Evan: and on network side, any cross-region replication for model embeddings or logs must not send raw data out of eu-west-2. we can allow metadata.

[00:04:00] Aria: That maps fine to Redwood's private deployment options. Briefly, we recommend envelope encryption for model outputs and stored artifacts: Redwood-managed data keys encrypted with your customer root key stored in your HSM. That way, we never see the unwrapped root. the per-object data keys are rotated at configurable intervals.

[00:05:12] Liam: On the audit side: we can surface key usage logs, key wrap/unwrap events, and administrative actions. For HSM-backed BYOK we rely on the cloud HSM or on-prem HSM audit trail; Redwood will also produce application-level logs with tamper-evident sequencing.

[00:06:30] Carlos: Two questions: 1) can we get cryptographic proof of deletion for keys? and 2) how does emergency key escrow work if we have to rotate keys mid-flight?

[00:07:05] Aria: For proof of deletion, we provide key destruction records from the HSM and supplemental application logs. The HSM typically returns a crypto handle that can be validated; some vendors support a signed attestation of destruction. For emergency rotation, we recommend a pre-negotiated key escrow policy where a split key or multi-party escrow is used - Redwood can support integration with your chosen escrow provider or run a temporary escrow with HSM-kept wrapped keys under strict SOPs.

[00:08:42] Priya: Is Redwood OK with a split primary key where two ops people hold shares and require quorum? we prefer that versus giving Redwood any single escape hatch.

[00:09:10] Jordan: That is fine. Redwood's private deployment model supports customer key sharding and split custody. The important part is the API for key unwrap/wrap operations and RBAC controls on who can request unwrapping.

[00:10:00] Evan: Are the unwrap calls visible in application logs? we need them to tie to our SIEM for forensic chains.

[00:10:18] Liam: Yes, unwrap/wrap and admin actions will be exported. we can push logs to your log collector via secure forwarder or to an s3 bucket in your account with SSE and designated retention. Note: there can be a slight lag for high-volume unwraps if we stream in buffered batches.

[00:11:30] Carlos: On TLS - we require mutual TLS for all service-to-service comms. Redwood hosted APIs currently support TLS; do you support mTLS and client cert rotation?

[00:11:56] Aria: We support mTLS in private deployments and Dedicated (customer can supply client certs). For hosted, we do optional client certs in the enterprise tier - but for your constraint we recommend Private with VPC peering or on-prem connector and mTLS enforced. Cert rotation is supported through a short-lived cert lifecycle and automation hooks - we have a cert-rollover runbook.

[00:13:20] Priya: Good. we also need to ensure tokens never leave our region - i.e., tokenization/kv cache that contains PII should be resident. how does Redwood ensure caching doesn't leak?

[00:14:01] Aria: Redwood offers per-tenant cache namespaces that can be pinned to a region. KV-cache is encrypted with tenant-specific keys and can be disabled if you prefer direct calls to disk. Also there's a cache TTL and strict memory purging on rotation. the caveat is performance impact when you disable cache.

[00:15:40] Evan: For KMS provider, we currently run an on-prem Thales HSM and also use Google Cloud KMS for some non-sensitive workloads. would Redwood integrate with on-prem HSMs?

[00:16:10] Jordan: yes, we support both cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and on-prem HSMs via our connector. The connector can be deployed in your network and does a key wrap/unwrap call to the HSM without Redwood storing raw keys.

[00:16:48] Aria: Important detail: the connector runs in a customer-provided VPC and uses mutual TLS to Redwood's control plane for signing requests. It only returns wrapped keys; the unwrapped material never leaves the HSM boundary. we also support PKCS#11-based HSMs and KMIP for legacy gear.

[00:18:12] Carlos: How are service accounts and SSO mapped? we use Okta and SCIM for provisioning. need RBAC tied to Okta groups.

[00:18:35] Liam: We integrate with SAML/SSO and can accept SCIM group sync. RBAC can be mapped to Okta groups so that only users in your security group can perform key admin operations. We also provide fine-grained API tokens for machine identities with short TTL and rotation hooks.

[00:19:50] Priya: Do your audit logs include the mapping from user identity to action, so we can reconcile with our Okta logs?

[00:20:05] Aria: Yes, logs include principal identifiers and OIDC subject identifiers; we recommend pushing both Redwood logs and HSM logs into your SIEM for full correlation.

[00:21:40] Evan: Performance question: unwrap latency - if every token unwrap requires an HSM call, that could add 30-80ms per call. how does Redwood mitigate this?

[00:22:02] Aria: We use cache of wrapped data keys (not the unwrapped root) in memory with strict TTL and LRU eviction; that avoids repeated HSM calls for hot keys. Also batching unwraps and async prefetch for predicted workloads reduces tail latency. We'll tune TTLs with you.

[00:23:30] Carlos: What about key rotation? we need quarterly rotation with zero downtime and automated rewrap.

[00:23:50] Liam: Our recommended flow is double-wrap: new data keys are generated and wrapped with new root key while old wrapped keys remain valid for a grace period, then we transition. The platform can do background rewraps and supports a canary rollout so you can validate before full cutover. We'll provide a playbook.

[00:25:10] Priya: For regulatory audits, we need evidence of who approved rotations and when. can Redwood include approval metadata in the audit trail?

[00:25:30] Jordan: Yes, approval attributes and ticket references can be attached to rotation events; we can add fields like approval_ticket and approver_id to the audit logs you receive.

[00:26:45] Evan: Suppose we need forensics after an incident. we need immutable logs for at least 2 years. what are retention options and WORM settings?

[00:27:05] Liam: We can push logs into your S3 with object lock/WORM enabled or into your SIEM with retention policies. Redwood stores short-term working logs for operational purposes but long-term retention is customer-controlled when you route logs to your account.

[00:28:50] Carlos: OK. question on cross-border key wraps: if we use cloud KMS in eu-west-2 but have a fallback region in us-east-1 for disaster, how do we avoid keys leaving geofence?

[00:29:12] Aria: Avoid cross-region replication of raw keys. For disaster we recommend a cold DR key material stored in a separate HSM under strict export rules or use multi-region keys with per-region roots that never replicate raw unwrapped keys. Redwood's routing policy can fail over to a compatible model variant in the same region or to a region with pre-approved key escrow.

[00:30:55] Priya: One more on BYOK: do you support Bring-Your-Own-Key with hardware import (i.e., import key material into cloud HSM) or only external wrapping?

[00:31:18] Aria: We support both approaches depending on the provider; some clouds allow importing key material into their HSM using import tokens, others require generating the key inside the HSM. For highest assurance, HSM-on-prem + connector is recommended so your key material is never generated outside your hardware.

[00:32:40] Jordan: quick note on compliance: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and maintains ISO 27001 controls in the corp plane - we'll send the artifacts. For hosted vs private you get different surface areas but we'll annotate the controls that map to your requirements.

[00:33:25] Carlos: In case of legal holds, can we freeze key rotation, and can Redwood enforce a hold on deletion?

[00:33:48] Liam: Yes, we can honor legal hold flags in the key policy - deletion requires an explicit multi-party approval and is logged. If keys are customer-managed in your HSM, physical deletion is under your control; Redwood will respect the hold by refusing attempts to rotate/delete until the hold is lifted.

[00:35:10] Evan: Networking: the connector needs access to HSM on-port 1792 in our data center behind NAT. are there firewall rules you need?

[00:35:30] Aria: We'll provide a minimal outbound list: control plane TLS endpoint, cert CRL endpoints, and NTP. The connector initiates outbound TLS so no inbound firewall holes are required. We can also support a one-way proxy if you need extra isolation.

[00:36:45] Priya: Let's talk about phishing and credential sprawl - we want short-lived API tokens and rotation automation. do you support ephemeral machine identities minted via our STS?

[00:37:10] Jordan: Yes, Redwood supports STS-style ephemeral tokens and can integrate with your STS provider for short TTLs. This reduces credential sprawl and ties into your audit story.

[00:38:40] Carlos: Any limitations on algorithms - we prefer AES-256-GCM and RSA-PSS for signatures.

[00:39:00] Aria: Those are supported. For envelope encryption we use AES-256-GCM for data keys and support typical signing algorithms for attestation. If you need post-quantum options we can discuss roadmap items.

[00:40:12] Evan: How does Redwood prove they never had access to plaintext? do we get crypto attestation or is it just a trust model?

[00:40:30] Liam: For on-prem HSM you get strong cryptographic assurances because the key material never leaves your HSM. For cloud KMS, we can provide KMS audit records and CloudHSM attestations where available. Additionally, we support signed key-wrapping statements and can include HSM-signed logs in evidence packs for audits.

[00:41:55] Priya: We also need a runbook for incident response - specifically steps to rotate keys, run rewraps, and roll back if needed.

[00:42:12] Aria: We'll produce a runbook with step-by-step commands for emergency rotation, canary validation, and rollback paths. We'll include CLI examples with PKCS#11 and cloud KMS commands.

[00:43:30] Jordan: mental note - Aria to draft runbook. Evan to share network diagram. Jordan to send SOC2/ISO.

[00:44:45] Carlos: About cost - does keeping keys on-prem or behind your connector add cost? we expect HSM vendor costs plus Redwood connector fee.

[00:45:05] Jordan: Correct - HSM vendor charges apply. Redwood charges a connector operational fee for maintenance and secure proxies; we'll send a price appendix. dedicated capacity has different pricing; we'll outline options in the follow-up.

[00:46:30] Priya: Any known gotchas with log correlation when using buffered export? we don't want gaps in log sequence numbers.

[00:46:48] Liam: Buffered export can introduce small delays but we include sequence numbers and checkpoints so you can detect gaps. We can also turn on synchronous streaming for audit-critical streams at the cost of throughput.

[00:48:10] Evan: For the demo/proof-of-concept, can we run a small pilot where Hightide provides an HSM and Redwood deploys the connector in our VPC to validate unwrap latency and the runbook?

[00:48:34] Jordan: Yes, pilot is the recommended next step. Typical pilot scope: connector deploy, sample key import, 1 week of unwrap/load testing, and a small audit extraction. We'll schedule with Aria and Evan.

[00:49:50] Priya: timeline expectations - we aim to be audit-ready by end of Q1. that leaves about 10 weeks. is that realistic?

[00:50:12] Aria: Yes, with a prioritized scope: pilot -> runbook -> expanded region lock-down -> final audit. We'll align milestones to your audit windows.

[00:51:30] Carlos: any final security concerns we should be aware of comparing Redwood to BigCloudAI? they advertise managed keys but we worried about key exposure.

[00:51:50] Jordan: Main difference is who controls the root. BigCloudAI often uses provider-managed roots by default. Redwood supports both but gives customers the option to keep roots in their HSMs and deploy connectors so raw key material never leaves customer perimeter.

[00:53:00] Priya: OK. recap please and next steps.

[00:53:12] Jordan: Recap: 1) Hightide prefers BYOK with on-prem HSM + Redwood connector, 2) mTLS enforced, 3) audit logs exported to your SIEM/S3 with WORM option, 4) key rotation runbook and emergency escrow options, 5) pilot to validate unwrap latency. Jordan to send SOC2/ISO docs, Aria to draft runbook, Evan to share diagrams.

[00:54:20] Carlos: Sounds good. anything else?

[00:54:30] Aria: I'll put together a short checklist for the pilot and include sample PKCS#11 calls.

[00:55:20] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites.

[00:56:00] Priya: Thank you. bye.

[00:56:10] Meeting end.

Notes/links referenced during call:
- SOC2 / ISO link (will be shared): https://redwood.example.com/compliance/pack/hts
